summary: The student has successfully created a functional Windows Forms Name Display application that meets the core functionality requirements. The app displays "Ben Schoolland" in a label when a button is clicked. However, there are some naming convention issues and a lack of code comments that could be improved.

requirementResults.requirement: Button triggers name display in a label
requirementResults.feedback: The button1_Click event handler correctly sets the label text to display the name when clicked.

requirementResults.requirement: Follow C# naming conventions (prefer CamelCase, avoid abbreviations)
requirementResults.feedback: Control name 'button1' uses default naming instead of descriptive CamelCase names. The label uses 'myLabel' which is better than default but could be more descriptive. Local variable 'myText' follows camelCase correctly.
The HelloWorld.cs file lacks comments explaining the button click functionality and the purpose of the variables.

issues.message: Button control uses default name 'button1' instead of descriptive CamelCase name like 'ShowNameButton'
issues.suggestion: Rename the control to something more descriptive like 'ShowNameButton' or 'DisplayNameButton'

issues.message: Label control name 'myLabel' could be more descriptive
issues.suggestion: Consider renaming to 'DisplayNameLabel' for better clarity

issues.message: Event handler method name uses default naming pattern
issues.suggestion: Could be renamed to 'ShowNameButton_Click' if button is renamed for consistency

issues.message: Missing comments explaining the button click functionality
issues.suggestion: Add comments to explain that this method displays the name when the button is clicked
Add comment explaining the purpose of the myText variable

positives: Core functionality works perfectly - clicking the button correctly displays the name in the label
Proper event handler implementation with correct method signature
Local variable 'myText' follows correct camelCase naming convention
Clean, simple code structure that is easy to understand
Uses appropriate data types (string for name storage)
The Program.cs file has good comments and follows standard Windows Forms application structure
